name_en: Zeitaku ni — desalted old takuan pickle simmered in dashi
summary_ja: 塩の抜けた古漬けのたくあんを水で塩抜きし、だし汁と醤油で炊き直した湖北地域の料理。漬物をわざわざ煮る手間のかかる料理であることが名の由来とされ、仏事に欠かせない定番として伝わる。
summary_en: Old, over-salted takuan pickle is soaked to draw out the salt, then simmered again in dashi and soy sauce. The name, meaning "extravagant simmer," is said to reflect the trouble of turning a pickle back into a cooked dish, and it remains a fixture at Buddhist memorial meals.
source_title: ぜいたく煮 滋賀県

name_en: Omi gyu no misozuke — Omi beef cured in white miso before grilling
summary_ja: 近江牛を白味噌に数日漬け込んでから焼く料理。江戸時代に彦根藩が薬用として将軍家へ献上した牛肉の味噌漬けが起源のひとつとされ、国内最古のブランド牛の歴史を今に伝える一皿とされる。
summary_en: Omi beef is cured in white miso for several days, then wiped clean and pan-grilled. One account traces it to the Edo-period Hikone domain, which presented miso-cured beef to the shogunate as a medicinal offering — an early chapter in the history of what is considered Japan's oldest branded beef.
source_title: 近江牛の味噌漬 滋賀県
